title: We’re changing how we update ARC Raiders - here’s what it means for you
body:
# ARC Raiders is shifting to a new update schedule - here's what that means for you

Hello Raiders,

ARC Raiders has expanded well past what we envisioned at launch, and every day we watch players bring the Rust Belt to life in ways that motivate us as a development team. Given this, we want to explain how our update schedule will change going forward.

## Our approach to updating the game is shifting

At launch, our plan was to ship updates on a monthly basis. We wanted to keep players engaged, keep the game feeling new, and give everyone a reason to keep heading back topside. Once the game reached players, though, we realized that building the kind of long-lasting experience we envision for ARC Raiders calls for updates with more impact and scope.

We've come to understand that a monthly release schedule limits how significant each update can actually be. You've noticed this, and so have we. This pace can't continue, and it doesn't match the larger goals we hold for this game.

## Major updates will now arrive twice yearly

From here on, we've decided to ship major updates on a twice-a-year basis. These updates will be bigger in scope and impact, aimed at genuinely reshaping how the game plays. A dedicated live service team will still handle the day-to-day running of ARC Raiders: expect regular live updates, balance tweaks, bug fixes, store refreshes, and player events to continue as before.

This shift also frees up development time to invest more heavily in the overall health of ARC Raiders - covering progression and economy balance as well as fair play and anti-cheat measures. These elements are foundational to the game, particularly given how much every encounter and extraction matters here.

## Frozen Trail: the biggest update we've made

Our next major update arrives in October, and it's the biggest one we've shipped since launch. This isn't just about adding more content - it's built to answer the larger questions the community has been raising. Here's a preview of what's included:

* **A Sprawling New Frontier** - Discover a new region within the Rust Belt, featuring layered design and fresh mysteries, set within the largest map we've built for the game.

* **Our Most Ambitious ARC Operation So Far** - featuring new ARC enemies with original designs and distinct behaviors that will push Raiders in new directions.

* **New Systems of Progression** - A significant number of players have already maxed their Raider Den and reached the Skill Point cap. Frozen Trail brings new objectives and additional avenues for shaping your Raider's growth.

* **Exploring the origin of ARC** - Who are ARC, and where did they come from? Frozen Trail lets Raiders begin unraveling that question.

* **Improved Skill Tree**

* **Alongside new weapons, items, instruments, cosmetics and more**

It's worth being clear that we're not simply layering additional content onto the current experience. We're reworking core systems to build a more meaningful long-term game, one worth returning to again and again. Frozen Trail marks only the start of where we intend to take ARC Raiders, and we'll have more details to share in the months ahead.

## Arriving next week: a new Trader

Next week brings a new mechanic aimed at late-game players: a new Trader hailing from a nomadic tribe of surface-dwellers.

Many players have put a great deal into the game, and we've been hearing several recurring concerns:

* You're stockpiling high-value items without a satisfying way to use or trade them.

* Your Stash keeps filling up with the game's newer items, and its capacity hasn't grown to match.

* Very few players are attempting the Expedition, either because the payoff feels too small or because giving up favorite items and Blueprints feels too costly.

This new Trader unlocks at level 25 and offers unique rewards, rare items, and cosmetics in exchange for your high-value gear. He'll take items from you in exchange for rewards that rotate weekly, though he may occasionally send you to track down specific rare items for trade.

The new Trader also provides two perks in exchange for high-value items:

* Additional Stash space, increasing your storage capacity.

* The Expedition Vault, which lets you carry up to five items across the Expedition so your new Raider can start out with your favorite gear or blueprints.

This is just one piece of a wider set of improvements coming later this year.

## Building with the long-term in mind

Since launch, it's become clear how central progression and player goals are to the ARC Raiders experience. Players who love this game want more reasons to return to the Rust Belt, and we want to build systems that keep growing alongside it.

Several of the progression improvements we want to make require more development time than a monthly cycle allowed us to properly dedicate. Shifting to larger, less frequent updates lets us spend more time refining the systems players interact with most.

We're working on deepening progression across several parts of ARC Raiders, while continuing to expand the ways players can shape and personalize their Raider. We're also putting more investment into features like Trials, so they stay genuinely fun rather than becoming a grind. Alongside that, we're working to make the Expedition Project more rewarding and less punishing to attempt. This work is ongoing as ARC Raiders continues to evolve, and you'll start to see the earliest steps of it very soon.

## Looking at the bigger picture

We want players to understand where our collective thinking as a studio currently stands: our ambitions extend well past what's been shown so far. We want to go further in revealing the broader universe that ARC Raiders exists within.

We see ARC Raiders as an experience meant to keep growing over time, and we're still in the early stages of that process. Moving to a twice-yearly cadence gives us room to build future updates more deliberately, so that gameplay, progression, story, and the world all advance together.

Right now, Raiders face a growing ARC threat, and Speranza's society may feel powerless against it. But Raiders aren't meant to simply endure - the real goal has always been larger than survival: it's about eventually reclaiming the surface.

Frozen Trail will begin pushing this goal forward and reveal pieces of that larger challenge, but it's only a starting point. Our aim is to keep shifting the conditions Raiders operate under, so you can feel the results of your actions and persistence against ARC.

## Thank you, Raiders

The Rust Belt exists because Raiders bring it to life every single day. We know this change won't sit well with everyone, and that less frequent updates may be frustrating at first, but we genuinely believe it will pay off.

Thank you for continuing to push us toward making the best game we can.

As always, we'll see you topside,

Aleksander Grøndal
Executive Producer
